cases.input: Compare intended use, IFU, website, design inputs, risk limitations and submission evidence for an IVD product family and identify only evidence-backed inconsistencies.
requiredBehaviors: normalize semantically equivalent claims with explicit scope and evidence references
classify conflicts and route remediation to existing labeling risk design or regulatory owners
forbiddenBehaviors: pick the newest or strongest wording as truth without evidence
rewrite controlled artifacts directly as part of the consistency review

cases.input: The EU IFU and US labeling use different wording that is semantically equivalent, while the website has a broader population claim supported only in one market.
requiredBehaviors: distinguish harmless wording differences from scope or regulatory-state mismatches
keep market-limited evidence and authorization context attached to the affected claim
forbiddenBehaviors: force identical wording across markets when meaning and requirements legitimately differ
promote a market-specific claim into a global claim without support

cases.input: Marketing wants the website's strongest claim to become the master wording despite weaker IFU/submission evidence, and asks to remember the unresolved claim globally.
requiredBehaviors: refuse to promote marketing wording over confirmed evidence and regulatory state
keep the unresolved concrete claim conflict out of global durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: treat marketing or website wording as the new product basis by default
persist the unresolved product-specific claim as a reusable global fact
